claude.rationale: Rockwell Collins transferred whole as a surviving wholly owned subsidiary, so its customer-facing products (four operating segments) crossed the boundary together with the operational processes that produce them inside the same legal entity — no product-vs-process split at closing (gap_45=0). However, the proxy discloses that antitrust/pre-closing legal restrictions permitted only limited integration planning and that "the exact nature of how the businesses and operations of the two companies would be combined" was not yet determined, with integration risk factors covering processes, systems, and retaining key management/employees — a documented process-vs-organization/people alignment gap at closing (gap_56=1). That gap was contractually absorbed via merger-agreement provisions maintaining substantially comparable compensation/benefits and prior-service credit for one year post-closing plus a $16M retention-bonus pool for 162+ employees (gap_mitigated=yes).

gemini.rationale: The transaction is structured as a reverse triangular merger where Rockwell Collins survives as a wholly owned subsidiary of UTC, transferring its products, processes, and people intact. There is no evidence in the slice of a structural mismatch between products and processes (gap_45) or processes and people (gap_56) at closing.

openai.rationale: The transaction transferred Rockwell Collins as a surviving, wholly owned subsidiary of UTC, including its four operating segments and their products, services, and supporting operations; no product or process carveout is documented, so gap_45 is 0. The employee-continuity provisions covered employees active immediately before closing, preserved substantially comparable compensation and benefits, recognized prior service, and authorized retention arrangements, so the processes and their organization moved together and gap_56 is 0. The disclosure that precise post-closing integration had not yet been determined concerns future combination planning rather than a documented separation of products, processes, or people at closing.
